summary: Prachi Vatsal is an Indologist and linguist who completed an M.Phil. and PhD at Jawaharlal Nehru University (2016–2023). In 2025, she held a position as a Sanskrit Educator at the Indian Institute of Technology Mandi.

Pradeep P. Gokhale is a scholar of philosophy, Buddhist studies, and Indology. He earned his Ph.D. from Savitribai Phule Pune University in 1980, where he later served as an Adjunct Professor in 2018.
Pragati Sahni works in Buddhist studies and philosophy, having studied under Damien Keown. She is attested as an Associate Professor at the University of Delhi in 2026.

Praggnaparamita Biswas is an Indologist who earned a Ph.D. from Banaras Hindu University (2008–2013) under Ratna Basu. She held posts at Ranaghat College (2013–2014), The Asiatic Society (2017–2021), and Dr. Babasaheb Ambedkar Open University (2021–2022).

Pragya Jain is an Indology and philosophy scholar who earned a PhD from Mohanlal Sukhadia University in 2021 alongside multiple other degrees. Her career includes posts at M. K. Sanghvi College, International School for Jain Studies, and Oxford Centre for Hindu Studies.

Prahlad Pradhan (1910–1982) was an Indology and Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Patna University and Visva-Bharati University. He served as a professor at Utkal University, principal at Gangadhar Meher University, and held posts at Ravenshaw College and other institutions.

Pramod Chandra (1930–2016) was an art historian and Indologist who earned his PhD from the University of Mumbai (1964). He served at Chhatrapati Shivaji Maharaj Vastu Sangrahalaya, as professor at the University of Chicago, and at Harvard University.

Pranabesh Bhattacharya is an Indologist and philosopher who studied at Ramakrishna Mission Vidyamandira, Visva-Bharati University, and Bankura University (Ph.D. 2025). In 2025, he became an Assistant Professor at Sri Sathya Sai University for Human Excellence.

Pranshu Samdarshi is a scholar of Buddhist studies, Indology, and history and archaeology. He earned an M.Phil. from the University of Delhi (2010–2018) and served as Assistant Professor at Amrita Vishwa Vidyapeetham and Nava Nalanda Mahavihara.

Prasanna Venkatesh T S works in computational fields and Indology. He has held positions at Ramakrishna Mission Vivekananda College as a Ph.D. Research Scholar and at the International Institute of Information Technology, Hyderabad.
Prasarn Lao-areun is a scholar of philosophy and Indology who studied under Viroj Inthanon and earned a PhD from the University of Mysore (attested 2014).

Prashant Dharmadhikari is an Indologist who held positions at K.G. Joshi College of Arts and N.G. Bedekar College of Commerce, and served as an Assistant Professor at the Central University of Gujarat in 2023.

Pratap Chandra Chunder (1919–2008) was a scholar in history, archaeology, and Indology. He was educated at Hindu School, Presidency University, and the University of Calcutta, where he studied under Prabodh Chandra Bagchi from around 1938 to 1941.

Pratapaditya Pal is a scholar of Indology, Tibetology, and art history who earned PhDs from the University of Calcutta and Cambridge. He held curatorial posts at the Museum of Fine Arts, Boston, Los Angeles County Museum of Art, and Chicago.

Praveen Verma is an Indologist who earned his Ph.D. from Jawaharlal Nehru University (1991–1997). He has served at the National Institute of Plant Genome Research since 1998 and as Adjunct Faculty at Jawaharlal Nehru University in 2020.

Prayag Raj Sharma is an Indologist and historian who served as a professor at Tribhuvan University (attested 1976–1990) and Dean at its Centre for Nepal and Asian Studies, as well as an editorial board member for Kailash.
Prayoon Mererk is a scholar of Buddhist studies and philosophy who completed his doctoral thesis at the University of Delhi in 1985 under the supervision of Margaret Chatterjee and Mahesh Tiwary.

id: P:Prince Peter of Greece and Denmark
summary: Prince Peter of Greece and Denmark (1908–1980) was a specialist in Tibetology and history/archaeology. He studied at Paris and the LSE under Bronisław Malinowski, and served in the Office of Strategic Services from around 1942 to 1945.

Pritam Saha is a scholar of philosophy, Sinology, and Indology who completed a Ph.D. in Chinese Philosophy at East China Normal University by 2025. In 2025, he was appointed a Postdoctoral Fellow at Sun Yat-sen University.

Priyanka Basu is an Indologist who studied at Bethune College. Her career includes posts as a curator at the British Library (2016–2021) and Lecturer in Performing Arts at King's College London beginning in 2021.
